# Goal: add rate limiting to the public search endpoint
<!-- EXAMPLE FILE — shows the quality bar of a contract generated by /goal.
     Note: every criterion is CHECKABLE; non-goals contain the drift; assumptions are declared. -->
Created: 2026-07-06 | Original request: "search is getting abused by bots, do something about it"

## Why (value)
Bots generate ~70% of the traffic on `/api/search` and degrade latency for real users.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Requests above 30/min per IP on `/api/search` receive a 429 — verification:
      new integration test `tests/api/rate-limit.test.ts` passes.
- [ ] The 429 response includes a `Retry-After` header — verification: assert in the same test.
- [ ] Authenticated users get a higher limit (120/min) — verification: a case in the test.
- [ ] The endpoint's p95 latency does not worsen by > 5ms with the limiter on — verification:
      `pnpm bench:search` before/after, numbers in the report.
- [ ] Full suite + typecheck green — verification: command output in the final report.

## Non-goals (out of scope for this round)
- CAPTCHA, fingerprint blocking, WAF — just the simple rate limit.
- Rate limiting on the other endpoints (separate proposal if this one works).
- Abuse-metrics dashboard.

## Constraints
- No new infrastructure dependency (use the Redis that already exists; do not introduce a service).
- Limits configurable via env var, with the defaults above.

## Declared assumptions
- "Abuse" = volume per IP (there is no evidence of a sophisticated distributed attack). If the
  logs show otherwise, I come back before implementing.
- A simple sliding window is enough (no need for an exact token bucket).

## Known risks
- Shared IPs (CGNAT) may limit legitimate users → mitigation: higher limit for authenticated
  users + monitor 429s during the first week.
- Redis unavailable → decision: fail-open (search works with no limit) — better to degrade the
  protection than to take down the feature.
